transcript: Ivy went away down Key Street toward the low town and the company yard, where the vans were. Kiva stood at the foot of the stair with her own sheets under her arm, which smelled faintly now of the company's tar and somebody else's lamp, and found she did not mind it. Ask held her left hand, at seven, by the north window, for two minutes by his watch. The loft was full of people dressing. Halden License was up at the south end, where Pettit was reading something aloud off a slip of paper, in a voice too low to carry. Old Four was arguing about who had taken whose boots. Selka Dre sat on the next bed to Seven's, with both feet on the floor, lacing a boot, and did not look round. Prue was on her own bed, with her hands held up in front of her in their ten little linen caps, waiting her turn. Perrin was sitting very upright on the end of his, in his shirt, with the strapping showing under it, being careful not to breathe.
